correctness.rationale: For the five-dimensional traceless upper triangular algebra b3(F_q) over each prime power q, quotienting the E13 ideal yields T⋉W with simple-root weights α=a-b, β=a+2b. Although E13 is not central in full b3, it is central in the nilradical; two independent W directions in the derived subalgebra bracket to E13, establishing quotient-generation equivalence. When char!=3, two weights are independent, giving rank(A,B)=2, rank(α,U)=2, rank(β,V)=2. At char3 coincident weights require rank(A,B)=2 and rank(α,U,V)=3. Counting independent uniform rows yields (1-q^-k)(1-q^(1-k))^3 or (1-q^-k)(1-q^(1-k))^2(1-q^(2-k)), respectively, including k=1 and nonprime q. A fresh independent full Lie closure enumerated F2 k2 96/1024 and F3 k2 0/59049; pinned checker also covers F4 and other seeds as corroboration. Thus minimal generator counts 2 and 3 follow algebraically, not from sampling.
residual_risks: Independent arithmetic experiments were confined to small q,k; the general proof depends on root weight decomposition and exact random-row probabilities.

evidence: Special linear results concern the full non-solvable sl3, Bulois counts tuples belonging to some Borel, not generating a fixed Borel.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Generation in an ambient simple algebra is not equivalent to generation of its solvable Borel subalgebra. Mere containment of a tuple in one Borel implies neither torus surjectivity nor simple-root span.
